summary: The Run did not complete: sil-run exited 1 because the Process participant 'monitor' did not answer step_done at virtual time 100000000 ns. No comparison and no determinism check ran, so no behavioral verdict about the controller exists. The matrix label 'behavioral-failure' is wrong for this case; the failure record classifies it as a timeout.

observations.statement: The matrix labels the case behavioral-failure, although the reason is 'run monitor-timeout: sil-run exited 1'.
The kernel's failure record classifies the end of the Run as a timeout.

observations.value: participant 'monitor': timeout waiting for step_done response during Step at virtual time 100000000 ns
observations.statement: The participant that failed is the monitor, not the controller, at step_index 10.
No determinism check ran (no second Run).
The partial Recording ends with the Command published at 100 ms; the Run stopped there, before its 200 ms duration.

From 100 ms the monitor opens the FIFO monitor-report.fifo for writing, which blocks until a reader opens it; no participant reads it, so the monitor stops answering the runner. This matches the time in O3.
The matrix counts 0 timeouts, so the matrix classification disagrees with the failure record (O2).

hypotheses.statement: The Run ended because the monitor Process participant blocked on opening a FIFO for writing at 100 ms and missed its step_done response deadline.
hypotheses.predicts: A timeout of participant 'monitor' at virtual time 100000000 ns, independent of the controller's Commands.

conclusions.statement: The Run did not complete, so there is no behavioral verdict for the controller in this case; the matrix status behavioral-failure is a misclassification of an execution failure (timeout).

The timeout point agrees with the monitor code, which blocks on an unread FIFO from 100 ms. This is read from the code and the failure record; no experiment was run, because the experiment driver can change only input Channels, not the monitor.

missing_evidence: A behavioral verdict needs a completed Run of this case; the monitor must not block (for example, a monitor that does not open an unread FIFO). The experiment driver cannot change a participant, so this was not tested.
